Mildred Gillars, nicknamed Axis Sally, was convicted of treason for working with the Nazis as a broadcaster.
Mildred Gillars ("Axis Sally") is convicted of treason.
Fulgencio Batista leads a successful coup in Cuba.
An anti-Chinese uprising began as thousands of Tibetans surrounded the Potala Palace in Lhasa to prevent the Dalai Lama from leaving or being removed by the Chinese army.

main.desc: Uprising in Lhasa, Tibet against China

events.text: Tibetan uprising: Fearing an abduction attempt by China, thousands of Tibetans surround the Dalai Lama's palace to prevent his removal.

main.desc: Uprising in Lhasa, Tibet against China

events.text: Thomas Playford, Premier of South Australia, left office after 27 years, the longest term of any democratically elected leader in the history of Australia.
Military prime minister of South Vietnam Nguyễn Cao Kỳ sacked rival General Nguyễn Chánh Thi, precipitating large-scale civil and military dissension in parts of the nation.

main.desc: Vice President of South Vietnam from 1967 to 1971

events.text: Military Prime Minister of South Vietnam Nguyễn Cao Kỳ sacks rival General Nguyễn Chánh Thi, precipitating large-scale civil and military dissension in parts of the nation.
British progressive-rock band Pink Floyd released their first single, "Arnold Layne".
Vietnam War/Laotian Civil War: North Vietnamese and Pathet Lao forces overwhelmed the American, Laotian, Thai, and Hmong defenders of Lima Site 85.
In Memphis, Tennessee, James Earl Ray pleads guilty to assassinating Martin Luther King Jr. He later unsuccessfully attempts to recant.
Vietnam War: Captain Ernest Medina is charged by the U.S. military with My Lai war crimes.
John Gorton resigns as Prime Minister of Australia and the leader of the Liberal Party of Australia after a secret ballot vote of confidence, being replaced in both positions by William McMahon.

main.desc: Prime Minister of Australia from 1968 to 1971

links.t: 1971 Liberal Party of Australia leadership spill

events.text: 1974 Belgian general election: Elections are held in Belgium for all 212 seats in the Chamber of Representatives, the Belgian Socialist Party taking the majority with 59.
Ho Chi Minh Campaign: North Vietnam began its final push for victory over South Vietnam with an attack on Ban Me Thuot.

main.desc: North Vietnamese campaign ending the Vietnam War

events.text: Vietnam War: Ho Chi Minh Campaign: North Vietnamese troops attack Ban Mê Thuột in the South on their way to capturing Saigon in the final push for victory over South Vietnam.

main.desc: North Vietnamese campaign ending the Vietnam War

events.text: Astronomers using NASA's Kuiper Airborne Observatory discovered a faint ring system around Uranus.
Astronomers discover the rings of Uranus.
1979 International Women's Day protests in Tehran: Protestor involvement peaks with 15,000 Iranian women and girls performing a three‐hour-long sit‐in at the Courthouse of Tehran.

main.t: 1979 International Women's Day protests in Tehran

events.text: Syzygy: All nine planets recognized at this time — Mercury to Pluto — align on the same side of the Sun.
Air Ontario Flight 1363, a Fokker F-28 Fellowship, crashes at Dryden Regional Airport in Dryden, Ontario, Canada, killing 24.
Eighteen months after seizing power, Prosper Avril was ousted as the military head of state of Haiti.
In Haiti, Prosper Avril is ousted eighteen months after seizing power in a coup d'état in September 1988.
1991 Salvadoran legislative election: The Nationalist Republican Alliance wins 39 of the 84 seats in the Legislative Assembly of El Salvador.
The Dot-com bubble peaks with the NASDAQ Composite stock market index reaching 5,048.62.
NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (artist's impression pictured) reached and entered orbit around Mars.
The Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter arrives at Mars.
The New York Times revealed that Eliot Spitzer (pictured), Governor of New York, had patronized a prostitution ring.
The impeachment of President Park Geun-hye of South Korea in response to a major political scandal is unanimously upheld by the country's Constitutional Court, ending her presidency.

Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 crashed six minutes after take-off from Addis Ababa International Airport due to a fault within the software of the plane, resulting in the deaths of all 157 people on board.

Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302, a Boeing 737 MAX, crashes shortly after takeoff, killing all 157 passengers and crew. This and the prior Lion Air Flight 610 led to all 387 Boeing 737 MAX aircraft being grounded worldwide.

2022 Hungarian presidential election: The National Assembly of Hungary elects former minister for Family Affairs, Katalin Novák, as president of Hungary in a 137–51 vote, becoming the first female president in the country's history.
Silicon Valley Bank collapses due to a run on its deposits, in the second largest bank failure in US history. Its operations are taken over by the FDIC.

links.t: List of largest bank failures in the United States

events.text: 2024 Portuguese legislative election: Elections are held in Portugal for all 230 seats in the Assembly of the Republic. The Partido Socialista loses its absolute majority to the Partido Social Democrata, winning 77 and 79 seats respectively.
Bam Adebayo of the Miami Heat recorded the second-highest scoring game in NBA history with 83 Points.

links.t: List of NBA single-game scoring leaders

events.text: Triumph of Orthodoxy: Empress Theodora II restores the veneration of icons in the Orthodox churches in the Byzantine Empire.
Arnošt of Pardubice becomes the last Bishop of Prague (3 March 1343 O.S.), and, a year later, the first Archbishop of Prague.

links.t: List of bishops and archbishops of Prague

events.text: Battle of Castagnaro: Padua, led by John Hawkwood, is victorious over Giovanni Ordelaffi of Verona.

main.desc: Battle fought in 1387 between Verona and Padua

events.text: Guaraní forces living in the Jesuit reductions defeat bandeirantes loyal to the Portuguese Empire at the Battle of Mbororé in present-day Panambí, Argentina.
The Frondeurs and the French government sign the Peace of Rueil.

main.desc: Civil wars in France between 1648 and 1653

events.text: Mount Etna in Sicily began erupting, eventually producing the largest lava flow in the volcano's history, and damaging Catania and other towns.

main.desc: Active volcano on the east coast of Sicily, Italy

events.text: The Daily Courant, England's first national daily newspaper, is published for the first time.
Queen Anne withheld royal assent from the Scottish Militia Bill, in the most recent veto by a British monarch of a bill that had been passed by Parliament.

main.desc: Queen of Great Britain and Ireland from 1702 to 1714

events.text: Queen Anne withholds Royal Assent from the Scottish Militia Bill, the last time a British monarch vetoes legislation.

main.desc: Queen of Great Britain and Ireland from 1702 to 1714

events.text: The signing of the Treaty of Mangalore brings the Second Anglo-Mysore War to an end.

main.desc: 1784 treaty which ended the Second Anglo-Mysore War

events.text: The Battle of Kharda is fought between the Maratha Confederacy and the Nizam of Hyderabad, resulting in Maratha victory.

main.desc: 1795 battle between Nizam and Maratha Confederacy in Western India

events.text: During a period of activity known as the Great Eruption, Eta Carinae (pictured) briefly became the second-brightest star in the night sky.

main.desc: Stellar system in the constellation Carina

events.text: Māori forces, led by chiefs Te Ruki Kawiti and Hōne Heke, attacked the British settlement of Kororāreka, New Zealand, beginning the Flagstaff War.

main.desc: Indigenous Polynesian people of New Zealand

Louis-Hippolyte Lafontaine and Robert Baldwin become the first Prime Ministers of the Province of Canada to be democratically elected under a system of responsible government.
The first performance of Verdi's Rigoletto took place at La Fenice in Venice (poster pictured).
The first performance of Rigoletto by Giuseppe Verdi takes place in Venice.
American Civil War: The Constitution of the Confederate States of America is adopted.
The Great Sheffield Flood kills 238 people in Sheffield, England.
Construction of the Seven Sisters Colliery, South Wales, begins; it is located on one of the richest coal sources in Britain.

main.desc: Village in Neath Port Talbot, Wales

events.text: Shō Tai formally abdicates his position of King of Ryūkyū, under orders from Tokyo, ending the Ryukyu Kingdom.
The Great Blizzard of 1888 struck the northeastern United States, producing snowdrifts in excess of 50 ft (15 m) and confining some people to their houses for up to a week.

main.desc: Severe snowstorm in the northeastern United States and Canada

events.text: The Great Blizzard of 1888 begins along the eastern seaboard of the United States, shutting down commerce and killing more than 400 people.

main.desc: Severe snowstorm in the northeastern United States and Canada

events.text: The Saint-Germain bombing ushers France into the Ère des attentats (1892-1894).
World War I: Mesopotamian campaign: Baghdad falls to Anglo-Indian forces commanded by General Frederick Stanley Maude.
In New York City, Samuel Roxy Rothafel opens the Roxy Theatre.
World War II: United States President Franklin D. Roosevelt signs the Lend-Lease Act into law, allowing American-built war supplies to be shipped to the Allies on loan.

World War II: The Empire of Vietnam, a short-lived Japanese puppet state, is established.

main.desc: Short-lived sponsored state of Imperial Japan in 1945

events.text: Rudolf Höss, the first commandant of Auschwitz concentration camp, is captured by British troops.

main.t: 1977 Washington, D.C., attack and hostage taking

events.text: After hijacking a bus north of Tel Aviv, Israel, members of the Palestine Liberation Organization faction Fatah engaged in a shootout with police, resulting in the deaths of 38 civilians and most of the perpetrators.

main.desc: 1978 hijacking of an Israeli bus by Palestinian militants near Tel Aviv

events.text: Coastal Road massacre: At least 37 are killed and more than 70 are wounded when Fatah hijack an Israeli bus, prompting Israel's Operation Litani.

main.desc: 1978 hijacking of an Israeli bus by Palestinian militants near Tel Aviv

events.text: Hundreds of students protest in the University of Pristina in Kosovo, then part of Yugoslavia, to give their province more political rights. The protests then became a nationwide movement.
Fifteen people are killed when Widerøe Flight 933 crashes into the Barents Sea near Gamvik, Norway.
Bob Hawke is appointed Prime Minister of Australia.

main.desc: Prime Minister of Australia from 1983 to 1991

events.text: The anime film Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind by Hayao Miyazaki was released.

links.t: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind (film)

events.text: Mikhail Gorbachev is elected to the position of General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, making Gorbachev the USSR's de facto, and last, head of state.

main.desc: Leader of the Soviet Union from 1985 to 1991

events.text: Lithuania declares independence from the Soviet Union.

main.t: Act of the Re-Establishment of the State of Lithuania
main.desc: 1990 declaration of independence from the Soviet Union by Lithuania

events.text: Patricio Aylwin is sworn in as the first democratically elected President of Chile since 1970.
The U.S. Senate unanimously confirmed Janet Reno as the first female United States attorney general.

main.desc: Upper house of the US Congress

events.text: The International Criminal Court holds its inaugural session in The Hague.
Madrid train bombings: Simultaneous explosions on rush hour trains in Madrid, Spain kill 191 people.

main.desc: Terrorist attack on Madrid's suburban trains

events.text: Michelle Bachelet is inaugurated as the first female president of Chile.
Georgian authorities accused Russia of orchestrating a helicopter attack in the Kodori Valley, in the breakaway territory of Abkhazia.
Space Shuttle Endeavour launches on STS-123, carrying the first component of the Japanese Kibō module to the International Space Station.
A teenage gunman engaged in a shooting spree at a secondary school in Winnenden, Germany, killing 16, including himself.
Winnenden school shooting: Fifteen are killed and nine are injured before recent graduate Tim Kretschmer shoots and kills himself, leading to tightened weapons restrictions in Germany.

Economist and businessman Sebastián Piñera is sworn in as President of Chile. Aftershocks of the 2010 Pichilemu earthquakes hit central Chile during the ceremony.
A massive earthquake and tsunami struck northeastern Japan and triggered a nuclear accident at the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant.

main.desc: Megathrust earthquake off Japan's east coast

events.text: U.S. Army soldier Robert Bales murdered sixteen civilians and wounded six others in Kandahar Province, Afghanistan.

main.desc: Land service branch of the U.S. military

events.text: A U.S. soldier kills 16 civilians in the Panjwayi District of Afghanistan near Kandahar.

main.desc: 2012 murders by a U.S. soldier in Afghanistan

main.desc: Business jet family by Canadair, later Bombardier

events.text: US President Joe Biden signs the $1.9 trillion American Rescue Plan into law.
The Burmese military kills at least 30 villagers, including 3 Buddhist monks, during the Pinlaung massacre in Shan State, Myanmar.
The Gothic king Vitiges ended his year-long siege of Rome, which was defended by the Byzantine general Belisarius
Vitiges, king of the Ostrogoths, ends his siege of Rome and retreats to Ravenna, leaving the city to the victorious Byzantine general, Belisarius.
Odo of Châtillon was elected as the 159th pope of the Catholic Church.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 1088 to 1099

events.text: Election of Urban II as the 159th Pope of the Catholic Church. He is best known for initiating the Crusades.

main.desc: Election of Catholic Pope Urban II

events.text: German city Munich (München) is first mentioned as forum apud Munichen in the Augsburg arbitration by Holy Roman Emperor Friedrich I.
Konrad von Wallenrode is elected the 24th Grand Master of the Teutonic Order (date is O.S.).

main.desc: 24th Grand Master of the Teutonic Knights (1391 to 1393)

links.t: Grand Master of the Teutonic Order

events.text: Croatian–Ottoman wars: After the execution of feudal lord Petar Kružić, Croatian forces at Klis surrendered to the Ottoman forces in exchange for their safe passage to northern locations.

main.desc: Conflicts between the Kingdom of Croatia and the Ottoman Empire

events.text: Start of the Siege of Maastricht, part of the Eighty Years' War.

main.desc: Part of the Eighty Years' War

events.text: Ignatius of Loyola and Francis Xavier, founders of the Jesuits, were canonized by Pope Gregory XV.

events.text: Ignatius of Loyola and Francis Xavier, founders of the Society of Jesus, are canonized by the Roman Catholic Church.

main.desc: Basque Spaniard Catholic priest and theologian (1491–1556)

events.text: James II of England lands at Kinsale, starting the Williamite War in Ireland.

main.desc: King of England, Scotland and Ireland from 1685 to 1688

events.text: Peninsular War: A day after a successful rearguard action, French Marshal Michel Ney once again successfully delays the pursuing Anglo-Portuguese force at the Battle of Redinha.

Paddle steamer Brother Jonathan docks in Fort Victoria (now Victoria, British Columbia), carrying smallpox-infected passengers from San Francisco. The ensuing epidemic killed an estimated two-thirds of First Nations in the province of British Columbia.
Andrew Watson (pictured) captained the Scotland national football team against England, becoming the world's first black international footballer.
The Girl Guides (later renamed the Girl Scouts of the USA) are founded in the United States.

main.desc: Organisations for girls and young women

events.text: At a ceremony at Kurrajong Hill, Lady Denman, wife of the governor-general Lord Denman, announced that the future capital of Australia would be called Canberra.

main.desc: City center and the location of Parliament House, Canberra, Australia

events.text: The future capital of Australia is officially named Canberra.
Moscow becomes the capital of Russia again after Saint Petersburg held this status for most of the period since 1713.

main.desc: Capital and most populous city of Russia

events.text: The Kapp Putsch begins when the Marinebrigade Ehrhardt is ordered to march on Berlin.

main.desc: 1920 failed coup in the Weimar Republic

events.text: The failure of the St. Francis Dam (pictured) northwest of Los Angeles resulted in a flood that killed 400 people.

main.desc: Former dam in Los Angeles County, California, US

events.text: In California, the St. Francis Dam fails; the resulting floods kill 431 people.
Mahatma Gandhi began the Salt March (pictured), a 24-day nonviolent walk to defy the British salt tax in colonial India.

links.t: History of the salt tax in British India

events.text: Mahatma Gandhi begins the Salt March, a 200-mile (320 km) march to the sea to protest the British monopoly on salt in India.
Great Depression: Franklin D. Roosevelt addresses the nation for the first time as President of the United States. This is also the first of his "fireside chats".
Supported by the Estonian army, Konstantin Päts staged a coup d'état, beginning the Era of Silence.
Anschluss: German troops occupy and annex Austria.

main.desc: 1938 annexation of Austria into Nazi Germany

events.text: The Moscow Peace Treaty was signed, ending the Winter War between Finland and the Soviet Union.

main.desc: Peace treaty signed by Finland and the Soviet Union on 12 March 1940

main.desc: 1939–1940 war between the Soviet Union and Finland

events.text: The most destructive train accident in Finnish history kills 39 and injures 69 people in Turenki, Janakkala.
The Battle of Java ends with the surrender of the American-British-Dutch-Australian Command to the Empire of Japan in Bandung, West Java, Dutch East Indies.

main.desc: Battle in the Pacific theatre of World War II

events.text: Cold War: U.S. president Harry S. Truman proclaimed the Truman Doctrine to help stem the spread of communism.

main.desc: 1947–1991 geopolitical rivalry between US and USSR

main.desc: 1947–1991 geopolitical rivalry between US and USSR

events.text: The Llandow air disaster kills 80 people when the aircraft they are travelling in crashes near Sigingstone, Wales. At the time this was the world's deadliest air disaster.
British diplomat Lord Ismay was appointed the first secretary general of NATO.
General Suharto (pictured) seized power from President Sukarno when the Provisional People's Consultative Assembly sworn him in as acting president of Indonesia.
Suharto takes power from Sukarno when the Provisional People's Consultative Assembly inaugurate him as Acting President of Indonesia.
Mauritius gains independence from the United Kingdom.

main.desc: Island country in the Indian Ocean

events.text: The Turkish Armed Forces executed a "coup by memorandum", forcing the resignation of Prime Minister Süleyman Demirel (pictured).
The 1971 Turkish military memorandum is sent to the Süleyman Demirel government of Turkey and the government resigns.
Tim Berners-Lee submits his proposal to CERN for an information management system, which subsequently develops into the World Wide Web.
Mauritius becomes a republic while remaining a member of the Commonwealth of Nations.

main.desc: Island country in the Indian Ocean

events.text: Several bombs explode in Mumbai, India, killing about 300 people and injuring hundreds more.
North Korea announces that it will withdraw from the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons and refuses to allow inspectors access to its nuclear sites.

links.t: Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons

events.text: Former Warsaw Pact members the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland join NATO.
Zoran Đinđić, Prime Minister of Serbia, is assassinated in Belgrade.
The World Health Organization officially release a global warning of outbreaks of Severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS).

main.desc: Specialized agency of the United Nations

events.text: President of South Korea, Roh Moo-hyun, is impeached by its National Assembly, the first such impeachment in the nation's history.
U.S. Army soldiers gang-raped a 14-year-old Iraqi girl and murdered her along with her family members.
In Mahmoudiyah, Iraq, 14-year-old Abeer Qassim Hamza al-Janabi is raped and murdered by five American soldiers of the 502nd Infantry Regiment, who also murder both of her parents and her sister.
Financier Bernie Madoff pleads guilty to one of the largest frauds in Wall Street's history.
A reactor at the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant explodes and releases radioactivity into the atmosphere a day after the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami.

main.desc: Disabled nuclear power plant in Japan

events.text: A gas leak caused an explosion in East Harlem, New York City, destroying two apartment buildings and causing eight deaths.
A gas explosion in the New York City neighborhood of East Harlem kills eight and injures 70 others.
US-Bangla Airlines Flight 211 crashes at Tribhuvan International Airport in Katmandu, killing 51 and injuring 20.
In the House of Commons, the revised EU Withdrawal Bill was rejected by a margin of 149 votes.
The United States suspends travel from Europe due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
Roman emperor Elagabalus is murdered alongside his mother, Julia Soaemias. He is replaced by his 14-year old cousin, Severus Alexander.
Election of Pope Felix III following the death of Pope Simplicius earlier that month.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 483 to 492

events.text: The Battle of Badr, the first major battle between the Muslims and Quraysh.

main.desc: First major battle in early Islam (624)

events.text: The Byzantine Empire and the Republic of Genoa sign a permanent treaty against the Venetians at Nymphaeum.

He besieges the city and finally, after a campaign of 8 months, Prataparudra surrenders on November 9.
A Spanish mercenary army surprised a band of rebels at the Battle of Oosterweel in the Habsburg Netherlands, beginning the Eighty Years' War.

main.desc: 1567 battle of the Eighty Years' War near Antwerp, present-day Belgium

main.desc: 1591 battle during the Moroccan invasion of the Songhai Empire

events.text: Harvard College is named after clergyman John Harvard.

main.desc: Undergraduate college of Harvard University in Massachusetts

The Battle of Cartagena de Indias (part of the War of Jenkins' Ear) begins.

main.desc: 1741 naval battle of the War of Jenkins' Ear

events.text: William Herschel discovered the planet Uranus from the garden of his house in Bath, England, initially considering it to be a comet.
William Herschel discovers Uranus.
Gustav IV Adolf of Sweden is deposed in the Coup of 1809.

Felix Mendelssohn's Violin Concerto receives its première performance in Leipzig with Ferdinand David as soloist.
Klemens von Metternich was forced to resign as the foreign minister of Austria following student demonstrations in Vienna.
The German revolutions of 1848–1849 begin in Vienna.
